test_scope: Two synthetic WebRTC peers in isolated browser contexts; no application login, matchmaking, real participant, or human capture device used.
browser: Chrome 157 via isolated Chrome DevTools contexts

credential_handling.source: TurnCredentialService in the authorized app container

peer_configuration.ice_servers: TLS TURN entry only; no STUN or UDP/TCP 3478 entries
peer_configuration.media: Canvas-generated video plus WebAudio oscillator track
peer_configuration.signaling: Gathered SDP exchanged manually between the two peer connections

candidate_pair_observation.browser_candidate_pair_state: in-progress while connection and inbound media counters were progressing
candidate_pair_observation.selected_boolean: false in this Chrome stats snapshot; relay-only policy plus connected state, nominated relay candidates, and bidirectional inbound media establish relay media flow

limitations: This proves browser-to-browser relay-only media transport through the configured TLS TURN endpoint, not the application WebSocket signaling, server allocator, API media receipt persistence, or event UI journey.
Chrome reported candidate pairs as nominated and in-progress rather than selected/succeeded in the sampled stats; no selected flag is claimed.
Synthetic sources do not validate physical camera or microphone capture.
